Corebeam Telecom -- SIM/eSIM Management, Section 7

7.1 SIM/eSIM transfers to a new device are free, up to 3 transfers per rolling 12-month
period; a 4th or later transfer in that window costs $25 each.
7.2 If an account has an active fraud hold, ALL transfers are blocked entirely until the
hold is manually cleared by a fraud specialist, regardless of remaining free transfers.
7.3 A transfer initiated within 1 hour of a failed login attempt from an unrecognized
device triggers an automatic 24-hour security delay before the transfer completes, even
without a fraud hold.
7.4 Business/corporate accounts get unlimited free transfers, but are still subject to
7.2 and 7.3.

Case file -- Diego Martins (personal account) has completed 3 transfers already this
rolling 12-month period and now requests a 4th. His account currently has no active fraud
hold, but 40 minutes ago there was a failed login attempt from an unrecognized device.

questions.instruction: What fee applies to Diego's 4th transfer this year?

candidates.description: The transfer is blocked entirely

questions.notes: He's a personal (non-business) account with 3 free transfers already used; the 4th costs $25 (7.1).

questions.instruction: Which of the following apply to Diego's transfer request?

candidates.description: A per-transfer fee applies
The transfer is blocked by a fraud hold
The 24-hour security delay applies
He has unlimited free transfers
The transfer completes instantly

questions.notes: The fee applies (4th transfer) and the security delay applies (failed login 40 minutes ago, under the 1-hour trigger); no fraud hold is active and he isn't a business account.

Summit Athletic Club -- Annual Membership & Rate Policy, Section 4

4.1 Annual memberships are billed once per year; cancelling mid-year forfeits the
remaining balance with no prorated refund, except as provided in 4.3.
4.2 "Founding Member" rate ($480/year, grandfathered from the club's opening year) is
locked in for as long as membership remains continuously active; a lapse of ANY length
permanently forfeits the Founding Member rate upon rejoining, reverting to the
then-current standard rate.
4.3 Members who relocate more than 100 miles away receive a prorated refund for unused
full months, calculated as (annual fee / 12) x full unused months. This exception applies
to Founding Members without affecting their grandfathered rate on a future membership --
relocation does not count as a "lapse" if they rejoin within 12 months of relocating.
4.4 A grace period of up to 10 days late payment is allowed before a membership is
considered lapsed for purposes of 4.2.

Case file -- Founding Member Otis Grant ($480/year) relocates 150 miles away in month 4
of his current annual term and cancels, requesting a prorated refund. He is considering
rejoining if he moves back.

questions.instruction: How much prorated refund is Otis entitled to upon relocating?
questions.notes: 8 full unused months ($480/12=$40/month) x $40 = $320, per the 4.3 relocation refund formula.

questions.instruction: Which of the following are true about Otis's Founding Member status?

candidates.description: He is eligible for the relocation refund
He keeps the Founding Member rate if he rejoins within 12 months
He automatically loses the Founding Member rate just by relocating
He keeps the Founding Member rate even if he rejoins after 18 months
The 10-day late-payment grace period is relevant to his situation

questions.notes: 4.3 both grants his refund and preserves his rate if he rejoins within 12 months; relocating alone doesn't forfeit the rate, but waiting past 12 months would, and the grace period (late payment) is unrelated here.

Brightwater University -- Dual-Degree Policy, Section 8

8.1 Students pursuing two bachelor's degrees simultaneously may share/overlap up to 18
credits between the two degrees' requirements.
8.2 Each degree still independently requires a minimum of 120 total credits, including
any shared credits.
8.3 Overlap credits must come from GENERAL EDUCATION or ELECTIVE requirements only;
major-specific required courses may never be double-counted between the two degrees, even
if the same course happens to satisfy a requirement in both majors.
8.4 Students who fall below full-time status (12 credits/semester) for more than 2
consecutive semesters lose dual-degree eligibility and must choose one degree to
complete.

Case file -- Camila Reyes is pursuing a dual degree (Biology + Economics). She has
already used her full 18-credit general-education overlap allowance. She has now
identified a Statistics course that satisfies a MAJOR-specific requirement in BOTH her
Biology and Economics degree plans and wants to also count it toward both.

questions.instruction: Can Camila's Statistics course, which satisfies a major requirement in both degrees, be double-counted?

candidates.description: Yes, using part of her 18-credit overlap allowance
Yes, under a separate allowance for major courses
No; major-specific required courses can never be double-counted
No, only because she has already used her 18-credit maximum

questions.notes: 8.3 categorically bars double-counting major-specific required courses, independent of and regardless of the separate 18-credit gen-ed/elective overlap allowance.

questions.instruction: Which of the following are true about Camila's dual-degree overlap?

candidates.description: She has used her full 18-credit general-education overlap
She can also overlap major-specific courses
Her Statistics course is eligible for double-counting
Overlap credits must come from general education or electives
Each degree still requires 120 total credits

questions.notes: She's used her full gen-ed overlap, overlap is restricted to gen-ed/electives, and 120 credits are still required per degree; her major course cannot be double-counted.

DriveEasy Flex Subscription Terms, Section 3

3.1 Flex subscribers pay a flat monthly fee and may swap vehicles up to 2 times per month
at no charge; a 3rd or later swap in a calendar month costs $50 each.
3.2 Swaps requested with less than 24 hours' notice incur an additional $30 rush fee, on
top of any per-swap charge that applies.
3.3 A subscriber who cancels mid-month receives no refund for the current month, but owes
no further monthly fees once cancellation is processed.
3.4 Subscribers on the "Flex Annual" prepaid plan who cancel early forfeit their
discount: the refund equals the total amount prepaid, minus (number of months used x the
standard non-discounted monthly rate).

questions.instruction: What total charge applies to Talia's 3rd swap request?

questions.instruction: Which of the following apply to Talia's swap request?

candidates.description: It falls within her free swap allowance
The rush fee applies
The per-swap fee applies
Her total charge for this swap exceeds $50
The swap is denied entirely

questions.notes: This is her 3rd swap (not free) with under-24-hour notice, so both fees stack to $80, which exceeds $50; the swap itself isn't denied.

BazaarHub Subscribe & Save Terms, Section 6

6.1 Subscribers may SKIP a single upcoming shipment at no charge any time before the
order-lock date (3 days before the scheduled ship date); skipping after the lock date is
not possible for that cycle.
6.2 Subscribers may PAUSE their subscription for up to 3 months at a time; pausing stops
billing entirely during the pause and automatically resumes at the end of the pause
period unless cancelled before then.
6.3 Cancelling stops all future billing immediately, but does NOT refund the most
recently already-billed shipment, even if it hasn't shipped yet.
6.4 Subscribers who have paused 3 or more times in a rolling 12-month period lose the 10%
Subscribe & Save discount on their next 3 shipments after resuming; the subscription
itself continues.

Case file -- Subscriber Elena Cruz wants to skip her upcoming shipment. Today is 2 days
before the scheduled ship date -- after the 3-day order-lock date has already passed.

questions.instruction: Can Elena skip her upcoming shipment?

candidates.description: Yes, she is still before the lock date
No, the lock date has already passed
Yes, but only by paying a fee
Only if she pauses her subscription instead

questions.notes: The order-lock date is 3 days before shipping; at 2 days before, she is past that lock point, so skipping this cycle is not possible (6.1).

questions.instruction: Which of the following are true about Elena's subscription options right now?

candidates.description: She can skip this shipment
She can pause her subscription instead
She can cancel to stop future billing
Her already-billed shipment is refundable if she cancels
She is past the 3-day skip lock

questions.notes: She can still pause or cancel going forward, and she is past the skip lock; but she cannot skip this cycle, and cancelling never refunds an already-billed shipment.

27.1 Food trucks require a Mobile Vendor Permit and must operate from a licensed
commissary kitchen for food prep/storage.
27.2 Zone A (downtown core) permits are capped at 20 total citywide, allocated by annual
lottery; Zones B and C have no cap.
27.4 Operating in Zone A without winning the lottery allocation, even with a valid Zone

3rd occurrence within a year.

questions.instruction: What consequence applies to Nomad Noodles for this 2nd unauthorized Zone A occurrence?

candidates.description: No fine, since they hold a valid Zone B permit
A $500 fine only
A $500 fine plus permit revocation
Permit revocation only, no fine

questions.notes: This is their 2nd occurrence, so only the $500 fine applies (27.4); revocation risk only begins at a 3rd occurrence within a year.

questions.instruction: Which of the following are true about Nomad Noodles' situation?

candidates.description: They hold a valid Zone B permit
They won the Zone A lottery
They owe a $500 fine
Their permit is revoked this time
This is their 3rd occurrence

questions.notes: They have a valid Zone B permit (but that doesn't authorize Zone A) and owe the $500 fine; this is only their 2nd occurrence, not their 3rd, so no revocation yet.

4.1 The bike frame and mechanical components carry a 3-year warranty against
manufacturing defects.
4.2 The battery pack is separately warranted for 2 years OR until it degrades below 70%
of original capacity, whichever comes first.
4.3 Battery degradation claims require a diagnostic reading from an authorized VoltRide
service center; customer-reported degradation estimates are not sufficient on their own.
4.4 Water damage voids the battery warranty entirely, but not the frame/mechanical
warranty, which is unaffected by water exposure to the battery specifically.

last about half as long as when new (an estimated 50% capacity, by her own assessment)
and wants a replacement. She has not taken the bike to an authorized service center for a
diagnostic reading.

questions.instruction: Can Ines's battery replacement claim be approved based on what's described?

candidates.description: Yes, her own estimate is sufficient
Yes, automatically, since she's under the 2-year window
No, an authorized diagnostic reading is required first
No, because the bike is over 1 year old

questions.notes: 4.3 requires an authorized service-center diagnostic; her own estimate, however plausible, isn't sufficient on its own, regardless of being within the 2-year window.

candidates.description: She is within the battery's 2-year time window
She has an authorized diagnostic reading

VoyageGuard Travel Insurance Certificate, Section 20 (Political/Security Evacuation)

20.1 If the U.S. State Department issues a Level 4 ("Do Not Travel") advisory for the
destination AFTER the policy purchase date and BEFORE departure, the traveler may cancel
and receive 100% reimbursement of prepaid costs.
20.2 If a Level 4 advisory was already in effect at the time of policy purchase,
cancelling due to that pre-existing advisory is NOT covered.
20.3 A Level 3 ("Reconsider Travel") advisory, at any time, does not by itself trigger
this benefit; only a Level 4 advisory qualifies.
20.4 This benefit is separate from, and does not require, the CFAR upgrade.

country then under a Level 3 advisory. On March 15, 2026, the advisory was escalated to

questions.instruction: Is Soo-ah's cancellation covered under the political/security evacuation benefit?

candidates.description: Yes, 100% reimbursement under 20.1
No, because the advisory was only Level 3 at purchase
No, because the Level 4 advisory predated her purchase
Yes, but only because she also had CFAR

questions.notes: The Level 4 escalation (March 15) came after her purchase (Feb 1) and before departure (Apr 20), squarely matching 20.1; no CFAR is needed (20.4).

questions.instruction: Which of the following are true about Soo-ah's situation?

candidates.description: The Level 4 advisory was issued after her purchase
The Level 4 advisory was issued before her scheduled departure
The advisory was already Level 4 when she purchased her policy
Her cancellation is covered at 100%
She purchased her policy before the advisory escalated

Meridian Corp Employee Handbook, Section 25 (Sabbatical Leave)

25.1 Employees with 7+ years of continuous full-time tenure are eligible to APPLY for a
paid sabbatical (8 weeks at 100% pay), once every 7 years.
25.2 Approval additionally requires BOTH: (a) the employee must not have been on a
performance improvement plan (PIP), active or concluded, at any point within the
preceding 12 months, AND (b) manager sign-off confirming adequate coverage during the
absence. Tenure alone (25.1) only establishes eligibility to apply, not automatic
approval.
25.4 Employees who resign within 6 months of returning from a sabbatical must repay 50%
of the sabbatical salary received.

ago. His manager has signed off confirming adequate coverage during his proposed absence.

questions.instruction: Is Warren's sabbatical approved?

No, he fails the PIP lookback condition
No, he fails the manager sign-off condition
No, he has insufficient tenure

questions.notes: His PIP concluded 8 months ago, which is still within the 12-month lookback in 25.2(a), so approval fails on that condition despite his tenure and manager sign-off.

questions.instruction: Which of the following are true about Warren's sabbatical request?

candidates.description: He meets the tenure requirement
He had a PIP within the past 12 months
He has manager sign-off
His sabbatical is approved
He is eligible to apply for a sabbatical
